title: US Panic: EU DUMPING Visa & Mastercard, Canada CUTS Treasuries, AI Bubble POP
speaker: Sean Foo

macro_themes.view: 10y above 5.3% and 30y heading to 6%; foreign holders (China, Japan, Canada) pulling back from Treasuries, and the trend will accelerate.
Administration refusing to admit inflation signals higher yields and pushes the Fed closer to hiking again.
EU payment consortium building an alternative to Visa/Mastercard; Europe pushing digital euro by 2029.
AI spending is a leverage loop (SpaceX debt for Nvidia chips, Nvidia vendor financing, Broadcom/Anthropic); high rates are the likely pin, but the bull run could last ~9 more months.

calls.reason: Treasury values crashing as foreign holders sell and inflation is denied; signals higher bond yields and possible Fed hikes.
calls.quote: it signals higher bond yields are coming at minimum, it really pushes the Fed closer to hiking rates once again

calls.reason: 30-year heading toward 6% amid a worsening bond crisis.
calls.quote: the 10-year is well above 5.3% and the 30-year is heading towards 6%.

calls.condition: Bull run can continue on rotation out of Treasuries; if yields keep rising or a hyperscaler cuts capex, the AI bubble could pop suddenly.
calls.reason: Money rotating out of Treasuries into tech stocks keeps equities elevated (cites Burry: ~9 more months of gains possible), but rising rates threaten the AI bubble.
calls.quote: to be clear, the current bull run in US stocks could continue for quite a while longer.

calls.reason: Demand inflated by circular/vendor financing (SpaceX debt-funded chip buys, $500B Nvidia vendor financing vehicle); if the bubble bursts capital evaporates.
calls.quote: this AI bubble is being inflated by the same companies that profit the most from that inflation.

calls.reason: EU consortium building a cross-border payment network threatens Visa/Mastercard dominance (~90% of EU cross-border card transactions).
calls.quote: Mastercard and Visa about to face a serious new competitor built entirely within Europe

calls.reason: Same EU payments-sovereignty threat as Visa.
calls.quote: the US monopoly over EU payment infrastructure could be under threat.

notes: Livestream; no date spoken, listing approx_date used. V/MA and NVDA biases are implied from the narrative (competitive threat / bubble), not explicit trade calls. 'Antropic'/'entropic' = Anthropic; 'Widow'/'BISM'/'Bankomet' are garbled names of EU payment firms (likely Bizum, Bancomat, Wero/EPI). SpaceX described as having Nvidia equity investment (garbled 'SP X').
